codexCategory.name: Shelter from the Scourge
codexCategory.description:
Month 1, Day 25
Another Blight will be upon us soon. It's just a matter of time. Everyone's already talking about where to flee depending on where the damned beast strikes.
Once again, no one listened. For the thousandth time, I argued in vain that the answer isn't to flee, but to hide. It's not impossible. This year I will convince them. I have to.
The answer isn't the roads, but underground!
|NEXTPAGE|Month 2, Day 2
As many people die in the fleeing as they do in the Blight. They die, they're exploited or enslaved, or a thousand other injuries to body and soul. Everyone carries the scars.
Everyone knows this, but nothing changes. People do the same thing every Blight with the same results, yet when I suggest something that breaks the cycle, they look at me like I'm the insane one.
I'm tired of a lifetime's worth of nightmares.
Fools!
|NEXTPAGE|Month 3, Day 15
I surprised Michelle with the news: I spent the money we had put aside for emergencies on the supplies we need to build our shelter. It was everything we had, but it was enough to get us what we needed. We can get it done if our family works together.
I told her this. She didn't listen.
She said I betrayed her. Damn her. She went running to her mother like she always does when we fight, taking the children with her. Why is she so willing to condemn them to the same horrors we've faced?
|NEXTPAGE|Month 3, Day 17
No more sulking. If I'm diligent enough and lucky enough, I'll build this shelter on my own. I'll convince Michelle and everyone through deeds, not words.
|NEXTPAGE|Month 4, Day 1
The Blight has begun. There's still so much more to do!
|NEXTPAGE|Month 4, Day 2
They've left with her family. She didn't even ask me to go. Tian protect them or Vismyr honor them. If that's what they choose, so be it. I'm too tired for the arguments anymore. What energy I have, I need for this.
I won't live this wretched cycle anymore.
I want to prove there's a world where our children can endure the Blight in safety. Not just prove, but show the way!
Please let me have enough time.

codexCategory.name: Marching Orders
codexCategory.description:
I Can't Stand Swamps.
If I never have to go trudging through another god forsaken swamp again for the rest of my life then I'll die a happy man. The captain has lost his mind! For some reason he insists on being "battle ready" by having us march multiple times a week through these insect infested pits. No amount of pleading with the man can reach him. In the last month we've had multiple men get infected with muck foot! One of them had to have their right foot amputated!
|NEXTPAGE|I swear to Tian the timing of this writing could not have been more apt! The captain has just barged in and demanded we get ready for the marshes with a shit eating grin on his face. He told us "you know the saying, Westmire Swampy Boys are prepared for anything!" but nobody says that. He made it up! One of these days I suspect the Captain is going to have to meet and unfortunate accident in the marshes.

codexCategory.name: Witch Light
codexCategory.description:
That Jack-fool of a brother of mine came in late last night, much later than usual. He'd been drinking with the other fools his age. He woke me to say they'd followed a blue light out onto the marsh. Said he'd met an actual woman there, one who fancied him. Neither part of that sounded right to me, but I was too tired to discuss it. Then this morning he started raving about the woman's beauty and I knew he was in trouble. Everyone knows not to follow a witch light, everyone who isn't a raving idiot, that is.
He was determined to go see her again tonight once it gets dark. Borrowed a clean shirt from somewhere, with frills around the collar. He'd gone from shy and bumbling to strong and confident overnight, and I don't think Love is behind this change. I fancied I could see it in his eyes, a tiny green flame where before was only dull shadow.
|NEXTPAGE|A week passed before he showed his face again, now as battered and bruised as the apple at the bottom of the cart. This woman's people, whoever they are- wanted something he wasn't willing to give, then they refused to let him go, and thrashed him for it. Anyway, he's free now and we wait to see who- or what- will come to collect him.
What a couple of weaklings we make, him with a pitchfork with one broken tine, me with the kitchen knife. But I'm not too worried. Surely my oaf of a brother can't be worth that much to them. I only wish the moon wasn't so high tonight, and so bright.

codexCategory.name: Lunatic Asylum
codexCategory.description:
My family told me I'd be miserable working at the Asylum, but it's turned out to be a total lark! Everyone here is just bazoomny, totally insane, staff and patients alike. There's a man here thinks he's a cheese wheel, that's a good laff! Everybody's rolling him around, racing him down hills and stairs. Good crack, like. Until he rolled into the ornamental pond and drowned. Quite a feat when the water's only eight inches deep, but I guess cheese can't swim, har!
|NEXTPAGE|Then there's Auntie Leona- she's got an obsession with cleaning! She'll clean anything- floor, pots, trees, whatever. She'll try and clean your clothes while you're still in them! Anyway, I've got brothers and sisters at home, I'm embarrassed to say how many, and they produce a LOT of laundry. So I borrowed a cart and started hauling it in, along with the curtains and linens and such. Old Auntie got so excited she hardly eats nor sleeps anymore, just clean clean cleans. Thinking about bringing in the neighbors' clothes next.
As for the staff, they've all got a side business with the Asylum as their base: taking bets on dogfights; loaning out patients for labor; they even turned one of the dormitories into a two-copper flop house!
|NEXTPAGE|Life here is just about perfect. The only worrisome bit is the massacre five years ago, when the lunatics all rose up in the night, barricaded the doors and razed the old place to the foundations with all the staff asleep inside. But I can't see something like that happening again.

codexCategory.name: On The Run
codexCategory.description: I don't know when it started, but my parents have been arguing about money. They try to talk in whispers, but our hut only has one room so I always hear everything. Papa owes a hundred gold or something to an ogre named Go-la-bag. He sounds really scary, so big his shadow can cover three strong men, with eyes like burning coals. Maybe his real name is Coal-bag. Why would papa want to work for an ogre? |NEXTPAGE|Today, Papa came home with his ear slashed almost in half. He tried keeping it under his hat but mama plucked it off him and got really upset. Then Papa said he tripped and fell under the plow, but I don't think she believed him. It's winter now and the harvest was over months ago. Mama said he couldn't work for the ogre anymore, but Papa said it was way too late. I don't know what that means, but I didn't ask or they would know I was listening. |NEXTPAGE|Papa woke us up early, long before dawn. It's worship day, but we're going to sneak away in the dark because that's the best time, Papa said. I could only take what would fit in the burlap sack I use for a pillow. I tried not to cry- they didn't see me cry, anyway. |NEXTPAGE|We sold our rickety old cart at the edge of the forest. A creepy old man was waiting to buy it from us, even though the sun wasn't up yet. Now we're walking, with Myna (our horse) carrying everything. The campfire at night is fun. I just hope Coal-bag doesn't get us.

codexCategory.name: Succumbing to the Blight
codexCategory.description: Hendrik is worse by the day. Some foul ailment has claimed his innards, and he is quickly exhausting what spare paper we brought along with us, in some vain effort to clean the cracks and crevices from whence his body is ejecting such fluids as I - for your own sanity - shall not describe here. I have felt a trembling in my own gullet as of late, though I know not if it is the result of whatever original malady has taken root within Hendrik or the byproduct of having witnessed the putrid fruits of it splattered all over our camp. We have already run through the paper I was going to use to continue our cartographical efforts, and Hendrik has threatened that the empty pages of this journal are next. So if my summation of this expedition continues no further than this, you can blame him.

codexCategory.name: Brother Blighted
codexCategory.description: My family has been lucky for a long time, but what we feared most finally came to pass: my brother got infected with the Blight. I know there's no hope for him, he's too far gone to join the Vanguard. I tricked him into the root cellar this morning; it was surprisingly easy. They all turn into dunderheads after the disease takes them. After I closed and locked the hatch, I could hear him bashing about but I wasn't concerned. The sharp angle of the stair makes it impossible to force the door from below. I waited until everyone was out of the house and I killed him. I had no choice. Any man could see it was an act of mercy. |NEXTPAGE|I'm trapped here now. The door's going to give at any minute. The hammering is relentless. They never stop. They never rest. The whole family, maybe the whole village, has turned. It's my fault and now I'm going to pay for it. The truth is, I couldn't kill him. He used to be my brother.

codexCategory.name: The Axident
codexCategory.description:
People of the vilage have allways hated Trogg!
They say Trogg stink! And Trogg ignerent! They say Trogg talk about self in third persin. But Trogg have his leters! Can some body be ignerent and have leters? NO!!!!
One day Derrik was taunting Trogg while Trogg chop wood, so Trogg throw axe at him as a funny joke. Derrik lost an arm. Everybody very MAD at Trogg!
|NEXTPAGE|Trogg haff to leeve vilage, but Trogg make new friend- a girl in black robes! A pretty girl! Except for missing eye. But she says it lost in combat because she is a ZOO-BYTE! Zoo-bytes like ded things and making more things ded. She invite Trogg to join Zoo-bytes, so Trogg leeve vilage forever. Trogg join Zoo-bytes in dark cave. Zoo-bytes smart! Trogg has smart frends! HAHAHA!!! Trogg told Zoo-bytes about axident when Derrik lost arm- Trogg need more practice, was aiming for neck.

codexCategory.name: Will of Adasil (1/4)
codexCategory.description:
The trials of the hero Surt Are shared at hold and drinking hall He forged through every wound and hurt To spare us ills that might befall
His sword cleft mountains numberless His shield held lance and claw at bay If evils showed, he found redress And never dodged the frenzied fray
Few know of Surt as he true was The fourth son of a poor millwright Who, with his cheeks bereft of fuzz Took up an axe one winter's night
|NEXTPAGE|The hounding wolves who stalked and crept Attacked a farmstead out of town In their defense, Surt's great axe swept And brought the wolven chieftain down
For Surt's heart harbored bravery To save a neighbor's life at cost He did not kill that wolf for free A finger from his left hand lost
How common must this tale be Each township owns their heroes same But Surt was destined balefully To have no peace, and too much fame

codexCategory.name: Will of Adasil (2/4)
codexCategory.description:
The bandits in the mountains near Wrought perils as the nights grew long And Surt, with bow and purpose clear Did hunt the blackguards for their wrong
A fiefdom sparked rebellion fierce Spurred on by faithless, godless dogs Surt's flowing spear, like hellions, pierced And quenched the villains' dialogues
Surt led a band, both bold and true To champion the common soul And when the dead rose, just those few Stood in their way and paid the toll
|NEXTPAGE|His martial prowess grew refined And bounties now were what he sought How many men did his hands grind To bring the karma he had wrought?
With sacks of gold, and burnished steel Did Surt return to home that day To hear the funeral bell peal And learn his line had passed away
Surt cast away his wealth and land And wept upon the hard clay road With heavy heart and shaking hand He locked himself in his abode

codexCategory.name: Will of Adasil (3/4)
codexCategory.description:
For years, he scarcely left his home Trapped in the silence and reflection His legend through the land did roam While he was lost in recollection
But then! A hammer broke his door And light and sun washed through the room The farmer's girl he'd saved before From wolves, broke through that dusted gloom
|NEXTPAGE|While Surt had grieved, her arm grew strong She bore a spear and shield and knife She hauled him out! With battle song Demanded he reclaim his life
The world had one last need of him To strike the Prince of Hamon-Sor His cup of blood had filled to brim And could not be borne anymore
So finally, Surt stood again And cast regret to the abyss To walk into the lion's den And earn a death not meaningless
|NEXTPAGE|He rallied men one final time To throw their lives into the storm Surt's heart was lifted, smile sublime To see the ranks and files form
Surt led this fearless regiment Upon a solemn, great crusade Their goal was of a single bent To see this daemon Prince unmade

codexCategory.name: Will of Adasil (4/4)
codexCategory.description:
The saga of his bloody path To Hamon-Sor is known by all What men hear is the aftermath They know naught of his mighty fall
While arrows sang and manflesh split His hands were fierce, he spun his blades With each new blow, each lethal hit The Prince gave him his accolades
|NEXTPAGE|When finally his great arms dropped The moment that the last men fell A rune shone on the heads he'd lopped And summoned forth a Beast from Hel
At last outmatched, he spied a glyph Bound twice to circles on the floor He pulled himself, legs growing stiff To sit on one amidst the gore
His shieldmaid sat opposed to him Both linking to the glowing rune She'd fought as well, but lost a limb The Beast would be upon them soon
|NEXTPAGE|As Surt bled out, the circle lit Hands grasped upon the Beast's foul mien They dragged it back into the Pit As if its threat had never been
And so, I write my final will With pride in death and more in life Sing songs of Surt and Adasil! He is my husband, I, his wife
Our bodies, here among our foes Will lie together faithfully I will not fight my eyes to close I'm coming, Surt. Please wait for me.

codexCategory.name: Frost Giants
codexCategory.description:
My family are woodcutters. We live far up in the Black Shard Mountains, by a stand of rare hardwood timber that earns us a good income.
In a pocket valley beyond our timber stand is a meadow that remains warm and green even after the first snowfall in the mountains. There is a delicious purple berry there that grows nowhere else. One day in the late autumn when I was ten, I suffered a sudden urge for those berries, as a child will, and took my little brother to collect some. It was much too late in the year to travel in the mountains, but my father was away trading, so I was certain I would get away with it.
|NEXTPAGE|The path to the valley was already waist-deep in snow and hard going, but we broke through to the meadow and ate those purple berries by the handful, until we felt sick. And we lay down at the base of a stunted mountain tree and slept.
When I woke up, the shock of the cold was like being cast in an icy pool. A sudden storm had blown down from the east and we were both blanketed in snow. We could see little beyond the footpath, and my brother immediately began to cry. Well, I was plainly fool enough to get us into this conundrum, I decided I must be clever enough to get us out. Even if my father would kill me later. |NEXTPAGE|I told my brother to start gathering fallen leaves, and when we both had as many as we could carry, we struggled back up the path as far as we could. Then with a hunk of bark I dug us a snug little snow cave, as my father had taught me, with a floor of wet leaves, and we huddled there to wait out the storm.
It was a long wait and when night fell we slept again, but fitfully, my brother kicking out every few minutes. Then I heard the heavy rumble of thunder. Unable to sleep and recalling my grandfather's stories, I crept out of our shelter to look at the mountains.
|NEXTPAGE|The storm was over, leaving the world stark and blue, and with every distant flash of lightning, I saw them cavorting about- the frost giants! What my grandfather had told us by the red light of the fire was true. A dozen of the monsters stalked up and down, wrestling and growling at each other and hurling boulders the size of houses. They were so gruesome I couldn't decide if they were at war or at play. I was paralyzed with awe.
The next I remember I was back in our snow cave, curled around my brother, waking to the first feeble light. The trek back would be cold and difficult, and I knew my father would hear every detail of our adventure when he returned. Except for the frost giants.

codexCategory.name: The Butcher
codexCategory.description: My father left for Dragate long ago, to defeat the Scourge forever, mama says. That's why he's been gone so long. We're not the richest folks in the village, but papa still sends us money, so we always eat well. Beef roast, fresh chicken, fish- there's always meat on the table. I only wish I didn't look so much like him. My mother is beautiful, everyone says so, but I am not. I'm big and shapeless, probably from all that meat; my nose is too round, bulbous is what the village boys call it; and my eyes are too narrow, so it always looks like I'm squinting. |NEXTPAGE|Anyway, ever since I was wee mama always sends me to the butcher to pick up our supper, and I cannot stand the man! He never misses a chance to stroke my hair or brush up against me. He's gotten even worse of late, calling me his little turnip, apple-cheeked lass and the like, but the thought of his ham hands anywhere near me makes me cringe. And he's so OLD!!! Today he winked at me. With his lump of a body, his fat nose and squinty eyes, I'd rather marry a skink. I hate him so much, I can't stop thinking about him, about that wink and that nose, and those eyes... Oh no.

codexCategory.name: Lostlorn Warrior
codexCategory.description: Hill or vale, ditch or dale, battle or rest, do I give up, or try to survive the test? when all is said and done, doesn't hope go with the setting sun? stay in place or go to assist, crawl home or fight in the mist, play it safe or take the risk, I've come so far, but is struggle truly my bliss? When all is said and done, what can be the effect of one? To fight in honor or to scamper away, to risk death or live another day, to boldly go or to meekly stay... My life is not worth so much, that I would save myself now, and dash my future away. When all is said and done... This battle means nothing, if the war is won. When all is said and done... when it comes to choices, I truly had none.

codexCategory.name: The Deserter
codexCategory.description:
My second husband is a hard man, fit from regular work, but when we met he knew next to nothing about running a farm. With the scars and his limp, I always suspected he'd been a soldier, but I was a widow and I needed someone. He was a good husband too, even-tempered, hardworking, but now some men from the town have come and arrested him. They call him a deserter- but a deserter from what? The two houses made peace months ago. Don't we have bloodshed and strife enough with the Scourge?
|NEXTPAGE|It's been a week with no word from town, and I'm falling steadily more behind. There's no way I can bring in the harvest without him. Then he returned in the darkest hour of night. He'd gotten free, he said, and stove in a man's head on the way, which means hanging for sure. He wanted me to run with him, into the hinterland, away from the village.
He's gone now, and again I am a widow with no husband. I'd never given any thought to such foolishness before, but I see now that I love him with all my heart.|NEXTPAGE|
I am waiting for the knock, when the soldiers come looking. I'll tell them the truth, for I've no idea where he's fled. They'll beat me, of course, if not worse.
I should have gone with him, there's nothing for me here. Why am I such a fool?

codexCategory.name: The Rightful Heir
codexCategory.description:
When my father died he was still a young man, and I not long out of my teenage years. As is the custom in the land, all property and rights passed to the eldest male heir, my hateful older brother, Eli. After he announced my immediate expulsion to the farmhands and other staff, I was driven from the property. I said a little prayer of thanks to Dyaena that they couldn't send the dogs after me. Those hounds loved me best of anyone.
My father's huntsman loosed a quarrel after me as I rode pell-mell across our fields and into the shelter of the trees. I believe he wanted to end me there, so my brother could stage a fatal encounter with highwaymen.
|NEXTPAGE|It was a heavy blow- I wouldn't even be allowed to attend my father's interment. His was a bizarre death, the kind of thing people blame on Fate or the gods. He was killed by a loose stone falling from a long disused watchtower at the edge of our land- but what in Caelum would bring him to that place? This is what I pondered as I set out on the road. Clear-eyed and with the spark of youth, I had thought I would simply make my way in the world, as younger brothers have had to do in folktales since the beginning of time.
But the world turned out to be a good deal harsher than I imagined, and a few months later I returned to the family estate in the dark of night. I am no thief- I meant only to gather a few possessions I'd been forced to abandon when my brother had me driven out.
|NEXTPAGE|The dogs came out to greet me and I was attempting to calm them when I was distracted by a dim light from the cemetery, not far from the main house. All my line was interred in the hilltop mausoleum there, the folly of an eccentric ancestor. Our grand plot was surrounded by the stones and monuments of wealthy townsfolk going back centuries. I decided to take a closer look.
The mausoleum door stood ajar!
|NEXTPAGE|I don't know what I thought I would find- my brother looting the dead of their rings and jewelry, perhaps?- but a stone panel had been shifted in the floor between the rows of caskets, to reveal a perilously steep stair. Gathering my courage, I descended the first few steps until I heard a shrill voice below. There was Eli, with his back fortuitously turned, in conversation with what seemed to be my father. What used to be my father.
|NEXTPAGE|He had been brought back somehow to a gray and ragged kind of half-life, and Eli was haranguing him about some hidden artifact or treasure. The corpse kneeled before him in abject defeat. The eyes were clouded white and dead, yet they still seemed to cut upwards at me, just for an instant. Whether it was the flicker of that doleful eye, or the uncertain light, I knew what I needed to do. I retreated to the mausoleum above and shifted the stone panel so it rested upright on the edge of the hole, firmly in my hands. And I waited.
|NEXTPAGE|When my brother returned to the stair and raised his light, I grinned down at him until I saw his surprise, then dropped the stone plate and dashed the brains from his head. Descending into the cellar, I found my father's cadaver was inanimate again. Thankfully Eli wasn't wizard enough to keep him in that unholy state.
My brother's fingers were heavy with rings, and I discovered the ancient grimoire he had used to work dark magic. After dousing the light and sealing the mausoleum again, I would sell these to generate some funds, and return a few weeks later. With my brother vanished I was now the rightful heir, and with my encouragement the huntsman and his cronies soon decided to move on to healthier climes.
|NEXTPAGE|I still think of my cursed brother occasionally, always in the darkest hours of the night. I am almost certain he murdered our father, and this eases my conscience somewhat. All that remains is to set the mausoleum right again, and return my father to his resting place.
One day.

codexCategory.name: Ramblings
codexCategory.description:
He's here, or at least close. I can feel it.
I'll find the way to reach him. I have to. They say it is forbidden but I care not about their rules, or whatever breaking them may cost me. The dark one will reward my actions.

codexCategory.name: True Arc Shield
codexCategory.description: Hello Adventurer! Whether you have slain me or come across my corpse by chance, congratulations! I have lived a full life, and defended my friends and family to see their futures flourish. I came to this dungeon to breathe my last breath, one way or another, but before doing so I hid my only material treasure, the True Arc Shield. My hope is that a brave and honorable hero may use it to ensure their loved ones live as long as I have (to at least a-hundred-and-forgot, exactly!) And if you're really lucky, you will too.

codexCategory.name: Lumella's Wings
codexCategory.description:
Yes I believe I have found it at last! The burial site of the great guardian Lumella! If this poem speaks truth I may find the help I need there. I have checked many records and I am certain that this village fell to plague over a century ago. I doubt there is still a threat of illness, yet it pays to be prepared. Once I have acquired sufficient medicines and antidotes to sate my worries I will travel there to confirm my suspicions. |NEXTPAGE|Where dawn's light kisses the shore She lays, waiting to rise once more
She fell at home to neither blade nor bow But from illness that struck flesh from bone
Buried in her tomb, nestled in the shore I pray that Lumella will light our way once more

codexCategory.name: Harland's Spyglass
codexCategory.description:
Having found what I came for, I was too hasty to leave and fell afoul of this trap. I'm not strong enough to prise the teeth apart, and every moment I grow weaker as the pool of blood around me expands. I am soon to die in this dark, awful place, but perhaps I can help you.
After years of exploration and toil I finally located Harland's Spyglass. It's the final location on my list, of course. Why is everything always in the last place one looks?

codexCategory.name: Chameleon Cloak
codexCategory.description:
My colleagues and I have found yet another point to disagree on. However many times I am proved right, they must try me again and again. They've invited a young apprentice to join our wizardly conclave. He smells of the gutter to me, but Mezzentious vouchsafed him so I kept my counsel to myself--much to my regret!
It was a matter of days before we discovered him stealing, and when we confronted the little rat, he had the stones to actually fight us! He held his own for several minutes, a confusing state of affairs, until I caught him with a bolt of dark magic.
He should have been reduced to ashes, but the blackguard shrugged it off and kept going. Shortly thereafter, he escaped.|NEXTPAGE|As for a slender youth fighting us to a draw, I think I already knew the answer by then. In addition to its other properties, the cloak is disguised as a dull, weathered garment, something you might see a grain merchant wearing. When I arrived home my fears were confirmed: my Chameleon Cloak had been stolen!
But we three are not quite as doddering as we appear. Unbeknownst to our thief, Colophon cast a simple cantrip of tracking before he slipped away, so we know exactly where to find him. I sketched out the location below so that later I may gaze upon it whilst savoring the thief's destruction!

codexCategory.name: Fleet-Footed Boots
codexCategory.description:
Dearest Brother,
I trust you recall me writing about Master Porvidius's "special orders," which have made him the richest cobbler within 50 leagues--well, the mystery is solved!
One fiercely cold night, I left the shop early, claiming a sour stomach, then circled back an hour later. All was dark and at first I thought the shop was empty, but the master was down in the cellar. That space is only used for storage, or so I thought.|NEXTPAGE|The bastard has an imp imprisoned in a secret room, trapped in a magic circle! He forces the creature to enchant his shoes and boots--not all of them of course, only one or two pairs of his finest every year. If the magistrates discovered Master Porvidius working this wicked magic he would be soundly flogged, and likely face a stiff fine. The latter would pain him more, I'm certain.|NEXTPAGE|Now I am the owner of a pair of enchanted boots, and instead of earning coppers as a lowly apprentice I plan to make my way in the world as a blackmailer! I've already packed my things and slipped away with the prize. But should the theft be reported before I have time to get my affairs in order, I hid the boots away. If anything happens to me, they're in a cave where I used to stop and sit for a quiet smoke when I needed to get away from the family. But I know how your memory can be, so I've attached a map just in case.
Yours in prosperity, Stephen

ability.name: Piercing Shot
ability.description: Loose an arrow at a single enemy.

ability.name: Shooting Stars
ability.description: Shoot a volley of arrows into the air. On his next turn, they fall and deal damage to occupants of the target cells.

ability.name: Guillotine
ability.description: Spin and strike all adjacent units, Rooting for 1 Round.

passive.name: Double Shot
passive.description: Act twice in a row if he begins his turn with no adjacent enemies. If he attacks a second time, the duration of status effects on him are reduced by 1.

ability.name: Viper's Strike
ability.description: Channel for 4 turns, then dash toward the furthest enemy, dealing damage and applying Death Terrain on the target and all cells along the path.

ability.name: Death From Above
ability.description: Jump into the air, crashing down 6 turns later, damaging adjacent cells and applying Death Terrain on them. If targets are Rooted, they are Stunned for 1 round.

passive.name: Free Rein
passive.description: Always act twice in a row. His second attack reduces the duration of status effects on him by 1.

passive.name: Death Terrain
passive.description: Viper's Strike and Death from Above apply Death Terrain on multiple cells. Occupants take 100 Dark damage at the end of their turn. Death Terrain does not expire, but can be overwritten by other terrain effects.

ability.name: Mark and Cleave
ability.description: Damage an adjacent target, Marking them for 3 Rounds.

ability.name: Low Blow
ability.description: Push back an adjacent target, inflicting Weaken for 3 Rounds.

ability.name: Leap Strike
ability.description: Jump forward into a vacant cell and damage a single adjacent target. If the target is Marked, inflict Bleed and Grievous Wounds for 3 Rounds.

ability.name: No Quarter
ability.description: Remove buffs on all adjacent enemies. Grant +5 Speed and +25 Critical Chance to self and adjacent allies for 3 Rounds.

ability.name: Disarming Strike
ability.description: Attack a single adjacent target, inflicting Weaken for 2 Rounds.

codexCategory.name: Bleed
codexCategory.description: Once per round, Bleed inflicts true damage (ignoring Defense) equal to 33% of the attacker's Power if the afflicted character performs any action other than Wait, Cleanse, or Bandage.

codexCategory.name: Blind
codexCategory.description: Evasion and Accuracy is reduced by 75%. The afflicted unit is unable to perform Attacks of Opportunity.

codexCategory.name: Burn
codexCategory.description: Once per round, Burn inflicts true damage (ignoring Defense) equal to 20% of the attacker's Power (stacking up to 3x). If a unit dies while Burning, Fire Terrain spawns in the same cell.

codexCategory.name: Charm
codexCategory.description: On their turn, Charmed units will attack their own allies. Taking damage breaks the spell.

codexCategory.name: Fear
codexCategory.description: When Feared, targets will flee to a new position. Their subsequent turns will be skipped until Fear expires or is removed. Taking damage breaks the spell.

codexCategory.name: Freeze
codexCategory.description: Frozen units are untargetable, unable to act, and can't take damage until the spell ends or the ice is destroyed.

codexCategory.name: Grievous Wounds
codexCategory.description: Afflicted units cannot be Healed, Shielded, or receive any buffs for the duration.

codexCategory.name: Mark
codexCategory.description: Marked characters receive 25% more damage from all sources.

codexCategory.name: Poison
codexCategory.description: Once per round, units suffer damage equal to 10% of their current Health.

codexCategory.name: Push & Pull
codexCategory.description: When moved by an ability, units suffer the Stagger condition for 2 Rounds. If they're moved into an obstacle or unit, the target takes damage. If they're moved into a pit, the target takes damage and is Stunned for 1 Round.

codexCategory.name: Root
codexCategory.description: Unable to move on their own or use abilities that incorporate movement.

codexCategory.name: Sleep
codexCategory.description: Sleeping units are unable to act on their turn or evade attacks. Taking damage breaks the spell. While asleep, they are healed a small amount.

codexCategory.name: Slow
codexCategory.description: Speed is reduced by 10. When applied, Slowed targets are moved to the end of the current round's turn order (if they haven't yet acted).

codexCategory.name: Stagger
codexCategory.description: Staggered units are unable to evade, critically hit, or perform Attacks of Opportunity.

codexCategory.name: Stun
codexCategory.description: Stunned units are unable to act on their turn. They can't evade, and their Defense is reduced by 50% for the duration.

codexCategory.name: Sunder Armor
codexCategory.description: Reduces the unit's Defense by 100% for the duration.

codexCategory.name: Taunt
codexCategory.description: Afflicted units are forced to attack the taunter on their turn, so long as the taunter and target are adjacent to each other. Taunted units can not perform Attacks of Opportunity on anyone but their taunter.

codexCategory.name: Weaken
codexCategory.description: The afflicted unit's Power is halved for the duration.
